prompt:
A cubic container of side length L = 0.30 m has rigid walls and contains N identical molecules of an ideal gas, each of mass m. The container is aligned with Cartesian coordinate axes x, y, and z.
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Diagram of a cubic container of side length L = 0.30 m aligned with Cartesian axes x, y, z. One molecule of mass m moves with velocity component u in the x-direction towards a shaded face of area A = L^2 perpendicular to the x-axis.]
(a) Consider one molecule moving with velocity component u parallel to the x-axis towards a face of area A = L^2 perpendicular to the x-axis. The molecule collides elastically with this face.
(i) State the magnitude of the change in momentum of the molecule during one collision. [1]
(ii) State the time interval Delta t between consecutive collisions of this molecule with the same face. [1]
(iii) Show that the average force F exerted by this single molecule on the face is given by F = (m u^2) / L. [1]
(b) Now consider all N molecules in the container.
(i) Explain why the total force F_x on the face is given by F_x = (N m <c_x^2>) / L, defining the symbol <c_x^2>. [1]
(ii) Using the assumption that molecular motion is random in three dimensions, derive the equation pV = (1/3) N m <c^2>, where V is the volume of the cube and <c^2> is the mean-square speed. [2]

parts.prompt: Using the assumption that molecular motion is random in three dimensions, derive the equation pV = (1/3) N m <c^2>, where V is the volume of the cube and <c^2> is the mean-square speed.

mark_scheme.criterion: (a)(iii) Shows F = Delta p / Delta t = 2mu / (2L / u) = (m u^2) / L
(b)(i) Explains that total force is the sum of forces from all N independent molecules: F_x = (m / L) * sum(u_i^2), and defines <c_x^2> = sum(u_i^2) / N, so sum(u_i^2) = N <c_x^2>
(b)(ii) States p = F_x / A = (N m <c_x^2>) / (L * L^2) = (N m <c_x^2>) / V
(b)(ii) Uses 3D random motion: <c^2> = <c_x^2> + <c_y^2> + <c_z^2> and <c_x^2> = <c_y^2> = <c_z^2> => <c_x^2> = (1/3) <c^2>, substituting to obtain pV = (1/3) N m <c^2>

part_enrichment.guidance: Initial momentum is +mu and rebound momentum is -mu. The change is (-mu) - (+mu) = -2mu; magnitude is 2mu.
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Stating mu or 0 instead of 2mu by forgetting the vector nature of momentum.

part_enrichment.guidance: The molecule travels distance L across the box and L back, giving total distance 2L between consecutive impacts on the same wall.
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Using L / u instead of 2L / u by forgetting the return journey across the cube.

marking_points.criterion: Shows F = Delta p / Delta t = 2mu / (2L / u) = (m u^2) / L.

part_enrichment.guidance: Apply Newton's second law: force equals momentum change per collision divided by time interval between collisions.
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Omitting the intermediate step showing the ratio 2mu / (2L / u).

marking_points.criterion: States F_x = (m / L) * sum(u_i^2) and defines <c_x^2> as the mean of the squared x-components of velocity, giving sum(u_i^2) = N <c_x^2>.

part_enrichment.guidance: Each molecule exerts force m u_i^2 / L independently. Summing over all N molecules gives (m / L) * sum(u_i^2) = N m <c_x^2> / L.
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Failing to explicitly define <c_x^2> as the mean of the squared velocities.

marking_points.criterion: Relates force to pressure: p = F_x / L^2 = N m <c_x^2> / L^3 = N m <c_x^2> / V.
Applies 3D isotropy: <c^2> = 3 <c_x^2> => <c_x^2> = (1/3) <c^2>, and substitutes to obtain pV = (1/3) N m <c^2>.

part_enrichment.guidance: Show the area division p = F / L^2, recognize L^3 = V, and apply <c_x^2> = (1/3) <c^2> based on random motion in three dimensions.
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Jumping directly to the factor of 1/3 without explaining that <c_x^2> = <c_y^2> = <c_z^2> due to random motion.

hints: In (a)(i)-(iii), trace the motion of one particle along the x-axis: distance 2L, speed u, momentum change 2mu.
In (b)(i), sum the forces of all N particles and use the definition of an average.
In (b)(ii), convert force to pressure using area A = L^2, and use 3D symmetry <c^2> = 3 <c_x^2>.
solution:
(a)(i) Magnitude of momentum change = 2mu.
(ii) Time interval between consecutive collisions = 2L / u.
(iii) Average force F = Delta p / Delta t = 2mu / (2L / u) = (m u^2) / L.
(b)(i) Total force is the sum of forces from all N molecules: F_x = (m / L) * (u_1^2 + u_2^2 + ... + u_N^2). The mean-square speed along the x-axis is defined as <c_x^2> = (u_1^2 + u_2^2 + ... + u_N^2) / N. Therefore, sum(u_i^2) = N <c_x^2>, giving F_x = (N m <c_x^2>) / L.
(ii) Pressure on the face of area A = L^2 is p = F_x / A = (N m <c_x^2> / L) / L^2 = N m <c_x^2> / L^3. Since volume V = L^3, p = N m <c_x^2> / V. In three dimensions, c^2 = c_x^2 + c_y^2 + c_z^2. Because motion is random, there is no preferred direction, so <c_x^2> = <c_y^2> = <c_z^2>. Therefore, <c^2> = 3 <c_x^2> => <c_x^2> = (1/3) <c^2>. Substituting this into the pressure equation gives p = (1/3) (N m <c^2>) / V => pV = (1/3) N m <c^2>.
teacher_walkthrough: Walk through each step of the classic Cambridge derivation logically.
Step 4: Summing over all molecules gives F_x = N m <c_x^2> / L.
Step 5: Pressure = F / A = N m <c_x^2> / V.
Step 6: Use 3D symmetry <c_x^2> = (1/3) <c^2> to arrive at pV = (1/3) N m <c^2>.
